Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
abstract: <jats:p>Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Education and Learning Technology

Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
abstract:
<jats:p>Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored.
Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes.
Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement.
Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization.
Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science

A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
abstract: <jats:p>The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)

title: HYBRID NETWORK INTRUSION DETECTION SYSTEM BASED ON SIGNATURE ANALYSIS AND MACHINE LEARNING METHODS
abstract: <jats:p>In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.</jats:p>

Cyber Defense Digital Twins: A Federated Learning and Zero-Trust AI Architecture for Autonomous Threat Prediction and Response
abstract: <jats:p>Modern enterprise networks operate under persistent threats that exploit cloud-native misconfigurations, identity sprawl, and API vulnerabilities at machine speed. Existing security operations center (SOC) architectures remain largely reactive, signature-dependent, and incapable of predicting multi-stage lateral movement. This paper proposes the Cognitive Cyber Defense Digital Twin (CCDT), a unified architecture integrating federated learning (FL), graph neural network (GNN)-based attack-path forecasting, adversarially hardened detection models, and autonomous Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) with deception engineering. The CCDT constructs a continuously synchronized digital replica of organizational assets and employs reinforcement learning-based red agents to stress-test detection models. A federated intelligence mesh enables cross-organizational privacy-preserving gradient sharing. Experimental evaluations against CICIDS-2018 and LANL datasets demonstrate 52% faster attack-path detection, 41% reduction in false positive rate, and 60% reduction in mean-time-to-respond (MTTR) compared to traditional SOC baselines. Integrated Explainable AI (XAI) modules using SHAP values enable audit-ready compliance reporting. The CCDT represents a paradigm shift from reactive monitoring to predictive, autonomous, and privacy-preserving cyber defense for hybrid cloud environments.</jats:p>

title: Transforming Education through Technology: The Case of COVID 19 Digital Learning in Nagaland
abstract:
<jats:p>Through the perspective of the COVID-19 pandemic and the disruption and opportunity it engendered, this chapter follows a transformative effect of EdTech and Digital education in India particularly in Nagaland through analysis. Drawing upon national policy frameworks, conceptual literature on educational technology, and contextual evidence based on the case of Nagaland, the chapter considers the rapid migration to digital learning as an emergency strategy (in response to the ongoing institution closures) based on the stark shifts in pedagogical practice, access to education services, and preparedness. The findings show that, including the ability of national programmes such as NEP 2020, SWAYAM, DIKSHA, PM e-VIDYA, and others, to promote access to digital tools was low within periphery or hill areas (e.g., Nagaland), due to lack of infrastructural resources, digital divide, unprepared teachers and economic/social divides, and more. The pandemic exposed the deep social and infrastructure divides in connectivity, device availability, assessment and learner engagement, with implications that were especially grave in rural and tribal settings. Although it accelerated the pace of innovation and the application of blended and low-tech learning practices teachers have been experimenting with digital platforms and the post-COVID recovery process, including remedial programmes and hybrid instruction. The chapter also discusses that blended learning is the most fitting, viable and sustainable approach for reaching the technological level in the field of educational technology at Nagaland. It implies that technology-mediated education can improve equity, quality, and resilience, but only under the conditions of inclusive policy design, strong digital infrastructure, vigorous teacher capability building, and culturally appropriate digital content.
Keywords: Educational technology, digital learning, COVID-19, Nagaland, online education, Challenges, blended learning</jats:p>

Clinical and Geometric Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence-based Organ at Risk Auto-contouring for Post-operative Oral Tongue Cancer Radiotherapy: Accuracy, Dosimetric Safety, and Workflow Efficiency.
abstract: Head and neck radiotherapy is among the most time-intensive planning workflows, particularly in countries like India with a high disease burden. Manual contouring of multiple organs at risk (OARs) along with target volumes contributes substantially to planning delays. Auto-contouring has the potential to reduce this workload, provided that geometric accuracy, dosimetric safety, and target coverage are maintained. Auto-contoured OARs using ETHOS treatment planning system (ETHOS TPS) were compared with clinically drawn contours using geometric metrics (dice similarity coefficient [DSC] and Hausdorff distance [HD95]) and dosimetric analysis in 40 postoperative tongue patients retrospectively. Mean OAR doses were recorded for both contour sets, and absolute dose differences were evaluated using paired statistical tests. Clinical relevance was assessed using Cohen's d with 95% confidence intervals. Agreement was quantified using Bland-Altman analysis, intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), and Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC). Target coverage and plan quality were assessed using PTV V95%, V105%, conformity index (CI), and homogeneity index (HI). OAR contouring time was recorded. Auto-contoured OARs demonstrated high geometric agreement with clinician-defined contours, with mean DSC values ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, HD50 ranged from 0.73 to 1.71 mm, and HD95 ≤ was 3.35 mm. Parallel organs such as the parotid glands and mandible showed minimal dosimetric differences and strong agreement (CCC up to 0.98, ICC up to 0.97). Serial organs demonstrated greater sensitivity to contour deviations, with spinal cord Dmax increasing by 1.98 ± 2.70 Gy (P < .001) and brainstem Dmax differing by -1.45 ± 2.41 Gy (P = .0005). Target coverage remained excellent, with mean V95% of 97.75 ± 1.22% for PTV60 and 98.16 ± 0.90% for PTV54, with high conformity (CI, 0.96 ± 0.01) and homogeneity (HI, 0.08 ± 0.01). Automated contouring reduced OAR delineation time to approximately 1.5 minutes per patient without editing and approximately 9 minutes with editing. Automated OAR segmentation demonstrated high geometric accuracy and preserved dosimetric integrity while significantly reducing contouring time. High geometric concordance translated into minimal dosimetric deviation for most parallel organs, whereas small contour discrepancies in serial organs such as the spinal cord resulted in greater sensitivity in maximum dose. Although serial organs require careful manual verification, integration of auto-contouring can substantially streamline radiotherapy planning workflows, particularly in high-volume head and neck oncology centers.

title: Mechanically robust solid electrolyte interphase via in situ adhesion of organic-inorganic bilayers for energy-dense lithium metal batteries.
abstract: The poor mechanical stability of solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) critically compromises the cycle life of practical lithium (Li) metal batteries, as repeated volume changes induce continuous SEI fracture and regeneration. Here, we propose a robust organic layer, in situ formed from 3‑glycidoxypropyltrimethoxysilane (GPTS) and anchored onto an inorganic underlayer, to enhance interfacial adhesion between the organic and inorganic layer, thereby improving the mechanical stability of the SEI. The epoxy groups of GPTS can polymerize in situ to form a robust organic layer, while the methoxysilane groups facilitate the anchoring of the organic layer onto the inorganic layer through chemical reactions. The elastic modulus of the formed bilayer SEI is much enhanced, thereby effectively mitigating its cracking and reconstruction during cycles. Li metal coin cells with GPTS-derived SEI deliver capacity retention of 80% after 290 cycles under practical conditions, which is 1.6 times higher than that of the coin cells with base SEI. A 5.5 Ah Li metal pouch cell with GPTS-derived SEI achieves a high energy density of 503 Wh kg

title: From aspiration to accountability: Human rights-based care and support for older persons at the UN Convention moment.
abstract: The emerging United Nations process toward a legally binding instrument on the human rights of older persons is not only a legal milestone; it is an accountability test for geriatric psychiatry, brain health, dementia care, mental health services, long-term care, community care, palliative care, digital systems, and implementation science. The legal protection gap has been documented through the Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing, the Open-ended Working Group on Ageing, OHCHR analyses, Independent Expert reports, and legal scholarship. As the Human Rights Council moves this work into an Intergovernmental Working Group to elaborate a legally binding instrument, geriatric psychiatry and allied fields have a responsibility to contribute clinical, ethical, scientific, and implementation expertise. This essay argues that the future Convention should be understood not only as a legal text but as an opportunity to make dignity, agency, legal capacity, supported decision-making, brain health, mental health, care, support, participation, and freedom from discrimination real in everyday systems. Ageism causes measurable health harms; mentalism and ableism compound exclusion; dementia and cognitive impairment can trigger diagnosis-based loss of voice and agency; grief, loneliness, coercion, and institutionalization reveal failures of supportive care; and artificial intelligence can deepen or mitigate ageism, digital exclusion, and epistemic injustice. Strengths-based approaches emphasizing wisdom, resilience, community capacity, and learning health systems offer a way forward. Building on the WPA-SOAP White Paper, Leiden Summary Statement, and WHO/OHCHR tools, this essay offers an implementation-focused bridge from principle to practice and from aspiration to accountability.

title: A fractional-order fixed-time attractive and noise-tolerant zeroing neural network and its application to robotic manipulator control.
abstract: Real-time and high-precision solving of time-varying problems is of great significance in fields such as robotic control and signal processing. As an efficient online method for solving time-varying problems, the Zeroing neural network (ZNN) has been extensively investigated. However, traditional integer-order ZNN models have inherent limitations in shaping convergence dynamics and accommodating non-local memory effects. To address these issues, a fractional-order fixed-time attractive and noise-tolerant Zeroing neural network (FO-FTNTZNN) is proposed, and its fixed-time attractivity in the Mittag-Leffler sense under noise-free conditions and its robust stability under bounded noise disturbances are rigorously demonstrated using a non-smooth fractional-order Lyapunov function. Furthermore, the attraction characteristics and anti-interference performance of the FO-FTNTZNN in both noise-free and noisy environments are further verified by multiple sets of numerical simulation experiments. Finally, the proposed FO-FTNTZNN model is successfully applied to the trajectory tracking control problem of a robotic manipulator. In summary, the proposed FO-FTNTZNN model provides a unified fractional-order framework for time-varying problem solving and robotic control, integrating fixed-time attractivity and bounded-noise robustness, and demonstrates its practical potential through numerical simulations and robotic trajectory tracking. A fractional-order parameter analysis is further provided as a supporting sensitivity study to characterize the memory-dependent dynamic behavior and transient response of the proposed framework.

Traditional integer-order ZNN models have inherent limitations in shaping convergence dynamics and accommodating non-local memory effects . To address these issues, a fractional-order fixed-time attractive and noise-tolerant network (FO-FTNTNNN) is proposed .

title: The illusion of continued leg growth: A modern 3D anthropometric analysis of segmental growth dissociation in Korean children.
abstract: The classical Anderson-Green model, which posits that male lower limb growth continues until age 17, often leads to overestimation of residual growth and subsequent overcorrection. We aimed to establish a modern, population-specific growth model for contemporary Korean children using 3D whole-body scanning. Through this comprehensive mapping, we investigated the physiological discrepancy and temporal dissociation between spinal and lower limb growth. High-resolution 3D automated anthropometric data from a large-scale national database (Size Korea; 1110 subjects aged 7-19 years) were analysed. Segmental growth trajectories were precisely isolated using standardized skeletal landmarks (knee and hip heights) and modelled via Monotonic Smoothing. A linear growth hypothesis for individual growth plates-validated through simulation analysis-was integrated into an interactive web application for adaptive residual growth prediction. Significant temporal dissociation was observed between spinal and lower limb growth. In males, lower limb growth plateaued at age 14.5-15.5, while standing height continued to increase until age 17.5-18.5. This 3-year discrepancy was driven exclusively by spinal growth continuing after lower extremity plate closure. Females showed a similar 2-year gap, with limb growth ceasing at age 12.5-13.5 and spinal growth at 14.5-15.5. The traditional "17-year rule" is a clinical illusion driven by late-adolescent spinal elongation. Modelling individual bone growth as a simple linear trajectory provides an intuitive, highly practical alternative that maintains predictive accuracy while minimizing clinical user error. These modernized, segment-specific references, combined with the customizable web interface, offer an evidence-based framework for optimizing the timing of leg-length discrepancy correction.

title: A deep learning model for detection and staging of osteonecrosis of the femoral head on x-ray images: a retrospective, large-scale, multicentre study in China.
abstract: Accurate detection and staging of osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) are essential for effective treatment yet frequently require specialist expertise and advanced equipment. To address this requirement, we aimed to develop a deep learning-based diagnostic model for the automatic detection and staging of ONFH using x-ray images, and compared its performance with clinicians to allow them to improve their diagnostic performance. In this retrospective, large-scale, multicentre study, we developed our deep learning model, Osteonecrosis Artificial Intelligence Diagnostician (OsteoAID), which was based on the You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) detection network and trained on a multicentre x-ray dataset. The dataset, dated from Jan 1, 2015, to Dec 31, 2023, and obtained from 16 399 patients across six Chinese tertiary hospitals, included 20 722 anteroposterior hip x-ray images of 28 785 hips, including hips with ONFH, healthy hips, and hips with other conditions radiographically similar to ONFH. To establish a rigorous ground truth for model training and evaluation, expert orthopaedists annotated each image to differentiate ONFH from confounding diseases and additionally classified the confirmed ONFH lesions on the basis of the Ficat and Arlet staging system. To verify the diagnostic performance of OsteoAID, we compared the model's accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, and area under the curve (AUC) with those of the original YOLOv8 model on the internal testing set for both the staging and detection tasks. Furthermore, the performance of OsteoAID was compared with the performance of radiologists and orthopaedists on two external testing sets, and its diagnostic performance was also benchmarked against MRI-the gold standard for ONFH diagnosis-with a third external testing set in which x-ray images were staged by corresponding MRI scans. Diagnostic metrics were compared with those of clinicians using t tests and McNemar's tests, with significance set at p<0·05. On the internal testing set, OsteoAID improved the staging accuracy from 87·42% (95% CI 85·88-89·20) to 96·44% (94·73-97·17) and the AUC from 88·54% (86·74-90·37) to 96·94% (95·75-97·98) compared with the original YOLOv8 model. For detection the model had a mean average precision of 92·97% (91·73-94·43) at an intersection-over-union threshold of 50%. In comparisons with clinicians on the external testing set I, the model showed staging accuracy of 96·60% (94·27-97·81), which was significantly higher than radiologists (74·96% [73·38-76·85]; p<0·0001) and junior orthopaedists (83·98% [81·27-84·06]; p<0·0001) and similar to that of expert orthopaedists (96·54% [94·18-97·79]; p=0·20). Furthermore, model-assisted diagnostics improved the accuracy of junior orthopaedists by an absolute difference of 12·70% and of radiologists by 21·47%. Although the accuracy improvement for expert orthopaedists was non-significant (an absolute difference of 0·74%; p=0·080), the diagnostic time was substantially reduced across all groups. On external testing set II (which included challenging cases: low-quality x-ray images affected by improper exposure, poor contrast, incomplete field of view, or foreign-object shadows, as well as smartphone photographs of x-ray films), the model showed robust performance even under extreme conditions, achieving an overall staging accuracy of 93·76% (93·09-95·82). Additionally, combining x-ray imaging with the deep learning model produced diagnostic results similar to MRI on external testing set III with an overall accuracy of 96·63% (95·68-97·86) and an AUC of 97·33% (96·65-98·75). The developed deep learning model shows expert-level diagnostic performance in the dual tasks of detecting and staging ONFH by use of anteroposterior x-rays, which can substantially enhance both the diagnostic proficiency and efficiency of clinicians. Consequently, the model could serve as a highly accessible decision-support tool to optimise clinical triage and guide appropriate treatment strategies. title: [Translated article] Complications associated with parenteral nutrition in hospitalized patients.
abstract: Malnutrition is common in hospitalized patients. Parenteral nutrition is a therapeutic alternative to meet the nutritional requirements of patients in whom the gastrointestinal tract is unavailable or non-functional. This therapy has been associated with a wide range of infectious, mechanical and metabolic complications. The aim of the study was to assess the incidence of these complications. A prospective multicenter observational study in hospitalized adult patients receiving parenteral nutrition ≥72 h was conducted. Follow-up was performed until one week after the discontinuation of parenteral nutrition. Data were collected from electronic medical records and parenteral nutrition validation programs (Kabisoft and Clinus). Risk of malnutrition was determined according to MUST or CONUT criteria. The main variables were: incidence of catheter-related bacteriemia, catheter-tip colonization, phlebitis, thrombosis, catheter obstruction, catheter malposition, pneumothorax, hyperglycemia, hypertriglyceridemia, hypercholesterolemia, hepatobiliary disorders and refeeding syndrome. A descriptive analysis was performed using SPSS v23 software. Sixty patients were included, with a median age of 68 (28-90) years, 48.3% men and a body mass index of 26.2 ± 6.6 kg/m Although complications associated with parenteral nutrition occur, the rate of serious complications, such as infections, is low. While most patients experienced at least one complication, metabolic events were the most common, and they are generally easy to detect and manage. The incidence of mechanical complications, mainly phlebitis and catheter occlusions, was moderate.

title: Identification of metabolic risk phenotypes among U.S. adolescents: A machine learning analysis of NHANES 2017-2023.
abstract: Adolescent metabolic risk is multidimensional and may not be fully characterized by individual anthropometric or biochemical indicators considered separately; however, evidence regarding data-derived metabolic-risk phenotypes among adolescents remains limited. To identify metabolic risk phenotypes among U.S. adolescents using unsupervised machine learning and examine demographic and socioeconomic factors associated with phenotype membership. Data from adolescents aged 12-17 years participating in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017-March 2020 and 2021-2023 cycles were analyzed. K-means clustering was performed among 848 adolescents with complete data for seven anthropometric and cardiometabolic variables. Logistic regression examined sociodemographic factors associated with elevated metabolic-risk phenotype membership. A two-cluster solution yielded the highest silhouette coefficient (0.289), identifying a lower metabolic-risk phenotype (n = 580, 68.4%) and an elevated metabolic-risk phenotype (n = 268, 31.6%). The elevated-risk phenotype was characterized by substantially higher BMI and waist circumference, together with higher triglycerides and LDL-C cholesterol, lower HDLC, and modestly higher glycated hemoglobin. In the adjusted logistic regression analysis (n = 763), older age was associated with greater odds of elevated-risk phenotype membership (aOR = 1.18, 95% CI 1.07-1.29), whereas income-to-poverty ratio was associated with lower odds (aOR = 0.78, 95% CI 0.70-0.87). Unsupervised machine learning identified two exploratory metabolic-risk phenotypes characterized by concurrent differences in adiposity, lipid, and glycemic measures. The findings provide an exploratory basis for investigating multidimensional cardiometabolic assessment approaches relevant to pediatric nursing. Independent replication and longitudinal validation are needed to determine their prognostic and clinical utility.
ai_summary: Adolescent metabolic risk is multidimensional and may not be fully characterized by individual anthropometric or biochemical indicators considered separately . Evidence regarding data-derived metabolic-risk phenotypes among adolescents remains limited .
